title: SpaceX Q3 2026 财报电话会要点：AI 算力业务成最大收入来源
content:
Rohan Paul 总结 SpaceX Q3 2026 财报电话会要点：Super Intelligence 算力租赁业务（客户含 Anthropic 和 Google）收入 $7.6B，近翻三倍于 Q2 的 $2.56B，超过 Starlink 连接业务的 $5.2B 成最大收入来源，其中 $608M 来自新收购的 Cursor。
原文梳理了 SpaceX 财报电话会的关键数字，AI 算力业务反超 Starlink 成为最大收入来源，读者可据此了解其业务重心转移。
SpaceX今日财报电话会议的主要要点
AI现在是SpaceX最大的业务：超级智能部门向包括Anthropic和Google在内的客户出租算力，带来了76亿美元收入，几乎是第二季度25.6亿美元的三倍。
这使其成为SpaceX最大的收入来源，超过了52亿美元的Starlink连接业务，其中6.08亿美元来自新收购的Cursor。
SpaceX扭亏为盈：净利润达到44亿美元，营收为146亿美元，增长161%，而一年前亏损11亿美元，第二季度亏损5.41亿美元。尽管如此，SpaceX在2026年前9个月仍显示净亏损4.13亿美元。
SpaceX与Tesla的合并正在研究中：两家公司的独立董事委员会应股东要求正在讨论合并事宜，Musk表示，作为存在利益冲突的一方，他被排除在这些谈判之外。他称合并是个好主意，但表示并不确定，任何交易都需要获得所有已发行Tesla股份的多数支持。
Musk预计收入将成倍增长：Musk预测到2027年底，年度经常性收入将达到5000亿至1万亿美元。SpaceX自身的近期指引则低得多，基于12月销售额，预计到2026年底年化收入为1000亿美元，2027年第一季度收入为330亿至370亿美元。
支出超过收入：第三季度资本支出达到196亿美元，其中164亿美元用于AI部门，SpaceX预计第四季度为350亿至400亿美元。Musk表示，SpaceX更倾向于短期算力合同，因为他预计随着AI模型改进，每瓦算力将带来更多收益。
Musk在孟菲斯工作：Musk表示，他经常每周在孟菲斯待4天，让Colossus II超级计算机上线，因为SpaceX每月增加约20万块Nvidia GB300芯片。截至9月底，算力容量为1.7GW，SpaceX预计到年底将达到2.5GW至3GW，Musk表示他有信心在2027年增加10GW。
路易斯安那州发射预计在2029年前实现：SpaceX最近宣布计划在路易斯安那州建设一座耗资1000亿美元的航天港，Musk表示内部目标是在两年内实现首次发射，而2029年极有可能，当年将实现规模化发射。
来源：Rohan Paul · x.com

report.summary: SpaceX’s Q3 2026 call reportedly shows AI compute leasing at $7.6B overtaking Starlink, but the extraordinary figures and Tesla merger talk need verification.
report.background: SpaceX historically earned most revenue from launch services and Starlink connectivity. The reported Q3 2026 results describe a sharp pivot: a “Super Intelligence” unit renting compute to customers including Anthropic and Google, plus the acquired Cursor, would make AI infrastructure the largest business. That shift fits the broader AI boom, where demand for Nvidia GPUs, power, and datacenter capacity has turned compute into a strategic utility. Musk’s xAI has built large GPU clusters such as Colossus, and SpaceX’s reported Memphis expansion with Nvidia GB300 chips reflects the industry’s race for gigawatt-scale capacity. However, the revenue, customer, acquisition, and Tesla merger claims are extraordinary and should be treated cautiously until confirmed by filings or company statements.
key_points: Reported AI compute leasing revenue reached $7.6B, nearly triple Q2’s $2.56B and above Starlink’s $5.2B. About $608M supposedly came from newly acquired Cursor, highlighting how coding tools can consume and resell large amounts of compute.

SpaceX reportedly swung to $4.4B net income on $14.6B revenue, up 161% year over year, versus prior losses. Yet the first nine months of 2026 still showed a $4.13B net loss, suggesting quarterly results may be volatile or one-off driven.

Capital spending reportedly hit $19.6B, with $16.4B for AI, and Q4 guidance of $35B–$40B. Musk reportedly prefers short-term compute contracts because model efficiency could raise revenue per watt, reducing exposure to long-term price declines.

Management guidance appears internally inconsistent: SpaceX reportedly targets $100B annualized revenue by end-2026 and $33B–$37B in Q1 2027, while Musk predicted $500B–$1T annual recurring revenue by end-2027 — far more aggressive than company figures.

Musk reportedly said Tesla merger discussions are underway through independent director committees, with him recused due to conflicts. He also claimed SpaceX adds about 200,000 Nvidia GB300 chips monthly and plans to scale from 1.7GW to 2.5–3GW by year-end.
report.impact: If accurate, the shift would reposition SpaceX from launch-and-connectivity provider to a major AI infrastructure landlord, intensifying competition with cloud providers and neoclouds for GPUs, power, and datacenter sites. Developers could gain more capacity and alternative suppliers, but short-term contracts and Musk-ecosystem concentration may bring pricing and continuity risk. Regular users would likely see more AI services scaling, yet also greater dependence on a few compute owners. The reported Tesla merger talk raises governance and conflict-of-interest questions. Given the unverified figures, investors and developers should wait for filings and audited disclosures before treating this as a durable market signal.
report.tools: To follow the compute buildout, watch vLLM and Ray for serving and orchestration, Kubernetes and Slurm for cluster scheduling, MLPerf for benchmarks, and Electricity Maps or WattTime for power and carbon data. Track Nvidia GB300 supply, xAI Colossus disclosures, and any SpaceX or Tesla filings for verification.
